barracks:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: pre-modeling room mockup for the first-person grid dungeon game Stone & Shadow, not a game screenshot or a finished asset. Create one wide landscape 16:9 image, a single coherent room view. Match the approved game interiors described here: warm grey-brown rough medieval stone block walls, large worn stone flagstone floor, flat dark stone ceiling, weathered dark oak furniture, muted iron, restrained burgundy and ochre accents. Subtle crisp low-resolution pixel-art surface detail over convincingly modeled three-dimensional forms; enough bevels, joinery and rounded pottery to feel solid, not crude ultra-low-poly blocks. Eye-level first-person camera just inside the entrance looking into the room, slightly angled so furniture depths and both side walls read clearly. Normal human furniture proportions and credible supports. Modest even warm ambient illumination with localized torch warmth, all furnishing details readable. Keep the floor uncluttered and circulation generous. No people, no UI, no interface frame, no lettering, no labels, no arrows, no grid overlays, no watermark. No photorealistic cinematic bloom, no glossy toy materials, no oversized furniture, no dark lines painted along every polygon edge. This is a practical modeling reference for approval, with separable reusable furniture rather than an architectural redesign.
Subject: a modest medieval dungeon barracks, rectangular room roughly five grid bays wide and seven deep, slightly taller ceiling than the kitchen. Exactly four single wooden beds: two along the left wall and two along the right wall, all lengthwise with the walls, headboards toward the far end. Each bed has real legs, substantial side rails, straw-filled linen mattress, a pillow, and a rumpled muted moss-green or faded burgundy wool blanket. Four modest iron-strapped wooden footlockers, one associated with each bed, placed at the foot without blocking the broad center aisle. Leave a clear cross-aisle halfway down the room and a clear path to a simple closed wooden door in the far wall. A few practical wall pegs with a cloak or belt, and a simple shelf with rolled spare bedding give the sleeping room a lived-in but orderly character. Two small iron wall sconces provide restrained warm light. The beds, bedding and footlockers are the focal objects; show their construction and proportions clearly. Keep the architecture plain and consistent with the approved stone rooms.

Subject: a compact square medieval dungeon armory, roughly five grid bays by five, with the same fairly low flat ceiling as the kitchen. An organized heavy wooden weapon rack is the focal piece across the far wall, holding a handful of individually readable spears, swords and axes; round and kite-shaped wood-and-iron shields are hung above or beside it. A waist-high sturdy wooden maintenance workbench sits against the right wall with a whetstone, a small oil jar, a folded cloth and one sword laid horizontally, plus a modest shelf of spare helmets and leather gloves above. One empty suit of practical grey steel plate armor on a restrained wooden stand sits against the left wall near the foreground: rounded closed visor helmet, breastplate, shoulder plates, articulated arms, split tassets and greaves, continuous lightly worn metal surfaces without a painted polygon grid. A small closed iron-banded equipment chest is tucked into the far-right corner. Keep the broad center floor and the path to a simple wooden doorway at mid-left completely clear. Two modest iron wall sconces illuminate the room. This is an equipment store and maintenance room, not a forge: no furnace, no huge anvil, no fire pit. Weapons, rack joinery, shield rims, workbench and armor should be clear, believable objects that can be modeled separately.
